title: Percentages, Ratio & Proportion
description: Apply percentages and ratio to compound interest, reverse problems, repeated change, direct and inverse proportion, and best-buy comparisons.

notes.heading: Percentages, Ratio and Proportion

illustration.alt: Diagram showing compound interest growth, direct and inverse proportion graphs, and a unit-price comparison for best buys.
illustration.caption: Percentages, ratio and proportion appear in finance, scaling and everyday comparisons.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
A percentage is a number expressed as a fraction of $100$. A ratio compares two or more quantities. Proportion describes how two quantities are related.

🔑 Key Concept
This topic brings together several important ideas:
• Compound interest: earning interest on interest.
• Reverse percentages: finding an original amount before a percentage change.
• Repeated percentage change: applying the same percentage change several times.
• Direct proportion: as one quantity increases, the other increases at the same rate.
• Inverse proportion: as one quantity increases, the other decreases.
• Best buys: comparing prices by finding a common unit.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Use multipliers to simplify percentage calculations.
• $1\%$ of an amount is found by dividing by $100$.
• Always check whether a question asks for the final value or the amount of change.

notes.heading: Compound Interest
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Compound interest is interest calculated on the original amount and on the interest already earned.

🔑 Key Concept
The formula for compound interest is:
$$A = P\left(1 + \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^n$$
where $A$ is the final amount, $P$ is the principal, $r$ is the annual interest rate and $n$ is the number of years.

💡 Worked Example
Maya invests £ $500$ at $4\%$ per year compound interest for $3$ years. How much is in the account after $3$ years?

Step 1: Identify the values.
$$P = 500, \quad r = 4, \quad n = 3$$

Step 2: Substitute into the formula.
$$A = 500\left(1 + \dfrac{4}{100}\right)^3 = 500 \times 1.04^3$$

Step 3: Calculate.
$$A \approx 500 \times 1.124864 = 562.432$$

Step 4: State the answer.
The amount is £ $562.43$ to the nearest penny.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using simple interest instead of compound interest. Simple interest would give $500 + (500 \times 0.04 \times 3) = 560$, which is less than the compound amount.

notes.heading: Reverse Percentages
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A reverse percentage problem asks you to find an original amount after a percentage increase or decrease has been applied.

🔑 How it works
If a value has been increased by $r\%$, divide by the multiplier $(1 + \dfrac{r}{100})$ to find the original.
If a value has been decreased by $r\%$, divide by the multiplier $(1 - \dfrac{r}{100})$ to find the original.

💡 Worked Example
A shop sells a jacket for £ $66$ after a $10\%$ increase. What was the original price?

Step 1: Find the multiplier.
A $10\%$ increase uses $1 + 0.10 = 1.10$.

Step 2: Divide the new price by the multiplier.
$$\text{original price} = \dfrac{66}{1.10} = 60$$

Step 3: State the answer.
The original price was £ $60$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Finding $10\%$ of £ $66$ and subtracting. This gives $66 - 6.60 = 59.40$, which is wrong because the $10\%$ increase was applied to the original price, not to £ $66$.

notes.heading: Repeated Percentage Change
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Repeated percentage change means applying the same percentage increase or decrease more than once.

🔑 How it works
Use a multiplier raised to a power.
For an increase of $r\%$ repeated $n$ times:
$$\text{final amount} = \text{original} \times \left(1 + \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^n$$
For a decrease of $r\%$ repeated $n$ times:
$$\text{final amount} = \text{original} \times \left(1 - \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^n$$

💡 Worked Example
A car loses $15\%$ of its value each year. Its original value is £ $20\,000$. Find its value after $2$ years.

Step 1: Find the multiplier.
A $15\%$ decrease uses $1 - 0.15 = 0.85$.

Step 2: Apply it twice.
$$\text{value} = 20\,000 \times 0.85^2 = 20\,000 \times 0.7225 = 14\,450$$

Step 3: State the answer.
The car is worth £ $14\,450$ after $2$ years.

✅ Check
After one year the car is worth $20\,000 \times 0.85 = 17\,000$. After the second year it is $17\,000 \times 0.85 = 14\,450$, which matches.

notes.heading: Direct Proportion
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Two quantities are in direct proportion when one quantity is a constant multiple of the other. As one increases, the other increases at the same rate.

🔑 Key Concept
Direct proportion can be written as:
$$y = kx$$
where $k$ is the constant of proportionality.
The graph of $y$ against $x$ is a straight line through the origin.

💡 Worked Example
Four pens cost £ $2.40$. How much do seven pens cost?

Step 1: Find the cost of one pen.
$$\text{cost of one pen} = \dfrac{2.40}{4} = 0.60$$

Step 2: Multiply by the number needed.
$$\text{cost of seven pens} = 7 \times 0.60 = 4.20$$

Step 3: State the answer.
Seven pens cost £ $4.20$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The ratio of the two quantities stays the same.
• Doubling one quantity doubles the other.
• $k$ is found by dividing $y$ by $x$.

notes.heading: Inverse Proportion
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Two quantities are in inverse proportion when one quantity increases as the other decreases, so that their product stays constant.

🔑 Key Concept
Inverse proportion can be written as:
$$y = \dfrac{k}{x}$$
where $k$ is the constant of proportionality.
Equivalently, $xy = k$.

💡 Worked Example
It takes $5$ workers $12$ days to build a wall. How long would it take $6$ workers at the same rate?

Step 1: Find the constant $k$.
The total work is $5 \times 12 = 60$ worker-days, so $k = 60$.

Step 2: Divide by the new number of workers.
$$\text{time} = \dfrac{60}{6} = 10$$

Step 3: State the answer.
It would take $6$ workers $10$ days.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using direct proportion and writing $\dfrac{5}{12} = \dfrac{6}{x}$. More workers means less time, so the relationship is inverse, not direct.

notes.heading: Best Buys
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A best-buy comparison decides which product gives the most for your money by comparing the cost per unit.

🔑 How it works
Divide the total price by the number of units to find the price per unit. The product with the lower price per unit is the better value.

💡 Worked Example
A $500$ g bag of rice costs £ $1.80$ and a $750$ g bag costs £ $2.55$. Which is the better buy?

Step 1: Find the price per gram for each bag.
$$\text{small bag: } \dfrac{1.80}{500} = 0.00360 \text{ per gram}$$
$$\text{large bag: } \dfrac{2.55}{750} = 0.00340 \text{ per gram}$$

Step 2: Compare the unit prices.
$0.00340$ is less than $0.00360$, so the large bag is better value.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always use the same unit when comparing.
• The larger pack is not always the best buy.
• Units may be grams, litres, items or any consistent measure.

questions.stem: Jake invests £ $800$ at $5\%$ per year compound interest for $2$ years. How much is in the account at the end?
questions.explanation: Use $A = 800 \times 1.05^2 = 800 \times 1.1025 = 882$, so the final amount is £ $882.00$.

questions.stem: A savings account pays $3\%$ compound interest per year. £ $2\,000$ is invested for $4$ years. What is the final amount to the nearest pound?
Which expression gives the value of £ $P$ invested at $6\%$ compound interest for $5$ years?
questions.explanation: The multiplier for $6\%$ increase is $1.06$, and it is applied five times, giving $P \times 1.06^5$.

questions.stem: A laptop is sold for £ $540$ after a $20\%$ increase. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: Divide by the multiplier $1.20$: $\dfrac{540}{1.20} = 450$, so the original price was £ $450$.

questions.stem: A coat is reduced by $25\%$ in a sale and now costs £ $45$. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: A $25\%$ decrease uses multiplier $0.75$. The original price is $\dfrac{45}{0.75} = 60$, so it was £ $60$.

questions.stem: A population of $40\,000$ increases by $8\%$ each year for $2$ years. What is the new population?
A house worth £ $150\,000$ loses $10\%$ of its value each year for $3$ years. What is it worth after $3$ years?
Five identical books cost £ $15$. How much do eight books cost?
questions.explanation: One book costs $\dfrac{15}{5} = 3$, so eight books cost $8 \times 3 = 24$. The answer is £ $24$.

questions.stem: $y$ is directly proportional to $x$. When $x = 6$, $y = 42$. What is $y$ when $x = 9$?
questions.explanation: First $k = \dfrac{42}{6} = 7$. Then $y = 7 \times 9 = 63$, so the answer is $63$.

questions.stem: A recipe for $6$ people uses $300$ g of flour. How much flour is needed for $10$ people?
questions.explanation: Flour is directly proportional to people. $\dfrac{300}{6} = 50$ g per person, so for $10$ people use $10 \times 50 = 500$ g.

questions.stem: $y$ is inversely proportional to $x$. When $x = 4$, $y = 9$. What is $y$ when $x = 6$?
It takes $8$ people $6$ hours to paint a room. How long would it take $12$ people at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Work is $8 \times 6 = 48$ person-hours. For $12$ people the time is $\dfrac{48}{12} = 4$ hours.

questions.stem: Which equation shows that $y$ is inversely proportional to $x$?
questions.explanation: Inverse proportion means the product $xy$ is constant, which can be written as $y = \dfrac{k}{x}$.

questions.stem: A $400$ g pack of cereal costs £ $2.40$ and a $600$ g pack costs £ $3.30$. Which is the better buy?
questions.explanation: $400$ g pack: $\dfrac{2.40}{400} = 0.006$ per g. $600$ g pack: $\dfrac{3.30}{600} = 0.0055$ per g. The $600$ g pack has the lower unit price.
